title: Enter in the search field searches
notes: Built in lane gap-search-cases. checks/parity/par-searchmac.py: case par-real-return-in-the-field-launches-the-typed-words (real_return_in_field, J2.1 step 'Return in the field runs the typed words'): the list's last row holds the keys, the socket's `key` opens the search (as par-keys.py:1416 does), the letters of 'hello' and Return are REAL key events (`keyevent`, KeyEventVerb.swift), the bar must say launched true with the words and the surface mac-search, and rows mac-main.quickreply.field must be empty; it is NOT JUDGED when the field has no cursor or the real letters did not land. Its positive control par-real-return-from-the-list-opens-the-reply: the same real Return with the list holding the keys opens the quick reply (Commands.enter), so the absence above means the field took the key. The mutant is ONE multi-line break of SearchField.swift lines 39 to 45 (the field's onSubmit AND onKeyPress(.return)): each alone stays green because the field has both routes. ⌘K is sent by the socket's `key`, not as a real event: the item is Enter in the field. par-searchmac.py main now prints one line per judged case (print_cases). Self-test model: GapModel (mutants return-ignored-in-field, return-reaches-the-list, list-return-dead). Case line numbers: grep -n 'REAL_CASES' checks/parity/par-searchmac.py.
